title: How many hours does the plane save?
description: A journey takes five and one sixth hours by train and one half hour by plane. The mixed number becomes a fraction, the two times get a common denominator, and the smaller time is taken from the larger.
teaching_notes: One idea: the time saved is the train time take away the plane time, so write the mixed number as a fraction and use a common denominator. Watch for students who take the half from the whole number five and forget the one sixth.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): a traveller decides on a destination for a vacation. By train it takes 5 1/6 hours. By plane it takes 1/2 hour. How many hours does the plane save?
video_script.why: A learner writes a mixed number as a fraction, as with the area of the bricks, and subtracts with a common denominator.
video_script.substitution: the book's own train journey of five and one sixth hours and plane journey of one half hour
video_script.anchor: a train journey and a plane journey drawn as two bars of different length
video_script.payoff_line: The plane saves four and two thirds hours.
video_script.fraction_reading: five and one sixth, thirty one sixths, one half, three sixths, twenty eight sixths, fourteen thirds, four and two thirds
video_script.design: Two bars, the long one for the train and the short one for the plane; the gap between their ends is the time saved.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a train bar and a shorter plane bar to the same destination

marks.train: the long train bar is drawn
marks.plane: the short plane bar is drawn below it
marks.ask: the gap between the ends flashes

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a traveller who picks a holiday destination.
<bookmark mark='train'/>By train the journey takes five and one sixth hours.
<bookmark mark='plane'/>By plane it takes one half of an hour.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many hours does the plane save?

beats.on_screen: the two bars stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: both bars cut into sixths of an hour; the plane bar covers three sixths

marks.sixths: both bars are cut into sixths of an hour
marks.half: one half of an hour covers three sixths
marks.gap: the gap between the two ends is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='sixths'/>To compare the two journeys, cut both into the same small parts.
<bookmark mark='half'/>One half of an hour is the same as three sixths of an hour.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The time saved is the gap between the two journeys.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the train takes five and one sixth hours and the plane takes one half hour.

beats.on_screen: To find: hours saved by the plane

marks.find: the words hours saved are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the hours the plane saves.

marks.frac: it turns into thirty one sixths

narration: <bookmark mark='mixed'/>Step one, write five and one sixth as a fraction, five times six plus one over six.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>That is thirty one sixths of an hour.

marks.sub: thirty one sixths minus one half is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>Step two, the time saved is the train time take away the plane time.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The denominators differ, so one half becomes three sixths.

marks.sub: the numerators are taken away over the same denominator six

narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>Step three, take away the numerators, thirty one minus three, over the same denominator six.
<bookmark mark='val'/>That gives twenty eight sixths.

beats.on_screen: 28/6: divide the top and the bottom by 2

marks.low: the numerator and the denominator are both divided by two

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step four, write twenty eight sixths in lowest form, by dividing the top and the bottom by two.

beats.on_screen: check: time saved + plane time = train time
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check that the time saved plus the plane time gives back the train time.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed in both forms

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The plane saves four and two thirds hours.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Twenty eight sixths and three sixths make thirty one sixths, which is the train time.
